sections.title: Accuracy depends on domain adaptation and granularity

blocks.heading: Domain adaptation
paragraphs: The same word can be positive in one industry and negative in another. We adapt models to your domain's language using labeled examples from your own data, and validate them on a held-out evaluation set.

blocks.heading: Choosing the right granularity
paragraphs: Overall document sentiment is quick to deliver; aspect-based sentiment takes longer but tells you exactly which features and moments drive satisfaction. We recommend the level that matches the decisions you need to make.

blocks.heading: Cost at volume
paragraphs: For high-volume feedback streams, fine-tuned models are usually far cheaper to run than large LLM APIs. We model running costs at your expected volume during discovery.

items.question: How much does a custom sentiment analysis system cost?
items.answer: Standard sentiment analysis typically costs $20,000–$45,000 and takes 6–10 weeks. Aspect-based sentiment analysis costs $30,000–$65,000 and takes 8–14 weeks.

items.question: What is aspect-based sentiment analysis?
items.answer: Aspect-based sentiment analysis measures sentiment toward specific features or topics within a piece of text — for example, positive about delivery speed but negative about packaging — rather than assigning one overall score.

items.question: Why not use an off-the-shelf sentiment API?
items.answer: Generic APIs are trained on general text and often misread industry vocabulary, product names and context. A domain-adapted model validated on your own data is typically more accurate, and can also be cheaper to run at high volume.

items.question: What data sources can you analyze?
items.answer: Product and app reviews, survey free-text, support tickets and chat logs, call transcripts, emails and social media posts — any text source you can provide access to.

items.question: Who owns the sentiment model?
items.answer: You do — model weights, code, labeled datasets and documentation are transferred at completion.
